title: QAMOO: Quantum Approximate Multi-Objective Optimization for Portfolio Management
abstract_summary: This preprint introduces Qamoo, a QAOA-based framework for discovering the full Pareto frontier in portfolio optimization across four objectives (expected return, risk, transaction costs, diversification entropy) using adaptive Dirichlet weight sampling, correlation-aware cost encoding, portfolio-structured mixers, and pre-trained QAOA parameters. The authors report hardware validation on IBM Quantum processors with improved hypervolume coverage and sample efficiency versus classical baselines, and present out-of-sample trading results with Sharpe ratios above 0.65.
methodology_description: The study formulates multi-objective portfolio selection as a binary asset-selection problem (x ∈ {0,1}^n) with normalized weights w = x/||x||_1 and four objectives (maximize expected return, minimize portfolio risk, minimize transaction costs, maximize diversification entropy). For Pareto discovery the authors apply weighted-sum scalarization with weights c sampled from a Dirichlet(1,1,1,1) distribution, build a QUBO encoding of the scalarized objective, map the QUBO to an Ising Hamiltonian (xi = (1 - zi)/2), and solve via the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). Key methodological features include: (i) correlation-aware cost-Hamiltonian encoding that emphasizes financially significant correlations, (ii) portfolio-structured mixer Hamiltonians that enforce sector diversification and cardinality constraints without penalty terms, and (iii) parameter-transfer learning using pre-trained QAOA parameters (β*, γ*) to avoid per-instance variational optimization. Circuits are designed for IBM heavy-hex topology (Rzz gates scheduled in three non-overlapping layers). The experimental pipeline iteratively samples Dirichlet weight vectors, constructs QUBOs, runs pre-parameterized QAOA circuits on either IBM Quantum hardware or MPS tensor-network simulators, decodes measured bitstrings to portfolios, evaluates the four objectives, archives solutions, and obtains a Pareto frontier by non-dominated sorting. Performance is reported using hypervolume, IGD, number of non-dominated solutions and runtime; comparisons are made against classical baselines (NSGA-II, MOEA/D, ε-constraint, randomized weighted-sum, DPA-a). Additional experiments explore QAOA depth (p up to 6), effects of hardware noise versus noise-free MPS simulation, and out-of-sample backtests of selected portfolios.
experimental_setup: Technology-sector portfolio with n=10 assets. 5,000 random Dirichlet weight vectors sampled (Dir(1,1,1,1)). QAOA circuits executed with 5,000 shots per circuit. QAOA depths p in experiments ranged from 2 to 6 (main reporting for p=3..6). Hardware backends: ibm_fez (156 qubits, Heron r2) and ibm_brisbane (127 qubits, Eagle r3) using a 42-qubit subgraph; MPS simulations run with bond dimensions χ = 50 and χ = 20. Pre-trained QAOA parameters (β, γ) used — no per-instance classical variational optimization reported.
dataset_used: A technology-sector portfolio of 10 assets. For each asset the inputs are expected returns (µ_i) and covariance matrix entries (Σ_ij); previous portfolio weights w_prev used for transaction-cost objective. The preprint does not specify external data provider or exact historical time window.

pipeline_steps: For each of M sampled Dirichlet weight vectors c ~ Dir(1,1,1,1):
1) Construct scalarized objective F(w; c) = c1(-f1) + c2 f2 + c3 f3 + c4(-f4).
2) Build QUBO matrix (Q, q) encoding the scalarized objective and domain-specific encodings (correlation-aware terms, portfolio-structured constraints).
3) Map QUBO to Ising Hamiltonian (h, J) via xi = (1 - zi)/2.
4) Instantiate QAOA circuit of depth p with pre-trained parameters (β*, γ*).
5) Schedule cost (Rz, Rzz) and mixer (Rx) gates respecting heavy-hex topology (Rzz applied in three color layers).
6) Execute circuit on chosen backend (IBM Q hardware or MPS simulator) with K shots.
7) Decode measured bitstrings into binary portfolios x and normalized weights w, compute objectives f1..f4 and add to archive.
After sampling loop: perform NonDominatedSort(A) to extract Pareto frontier approximation P.

results_summary: The preprint introduces Qamoo, a QAOA-based framework for multi-objective portfolio optimization that uses stochastic Dirichlet weight sampling and pre-trained QAOA parameters to produce diverse portfolio selections. The authors report experimental validation on IBM Quantum hardware for a 10-asset technology-sector portfolio, claiming superior Pareto-front coverage (3.2% higher hypervolume than NSGA-II), substantially fewer objective evaluations (10×), and practical backtest performance (Sharpe ratios ≥ 0.65) for selected portfolios. Additional contributions include correlation-aware encoding, portfolio-structured mixers, and a production-oriented system architecture. Some methodological claims (e.g., mixer effectiveness without penalties, general production scalability) are proposed but not exhaustively validated in the preprint.

key_ideas: #idea:quantum-advantage — QAMOO (QAOA-based) is used to approximate the Pareto frontier for a 4-objective portfolio problem and is reported to achieve higher hypervolume (e.g., +3.2% vs NSGA-II) and improved sample-efficiency (10x fewer objective evaluations) on the tested 10-asset instance.

#idea:near-term-feasibility — The approach is demonstrated on IBM Quantum hardware (42-qubit subgraph on larger devices) and MPS tensor-network simulators (χ=20,50), with QAOA depths p up to 6 and pre-trained parameters enabling execution without per-instance variational optimization.

#idea:hybrid-approach — Classical components include Dirichlet-weight sampling for scalarizations, QUBO construction and post-processing (non-dominated sorting), plus parameter-transfer learning (pre-trained β*, γ*) to avoid per-instance classical optimization, forming a quantum-classical pipeline.

#idea:quantum-advantage — Domain-aware engineering: correlation-aware cost-Hamiltonian encoding and portfolio-structured mixer Hamiltonians are introduced to enforce sector diversification and cardinality constraints natively in the circuit rather than via penalty terms.

#idea:quantum-advantage — The authors present out-of-sample backtests for selected QAMOO portfolios with reported Sharpe ratios >0.65, and report metrics including HV, IGD, number of nondominated solutions and runtime comparisons to standard MOEAs.
#limitation:qubit-count — Experiments are limited to a 10-asset universe and a 42-qubit subgraph; scaling implications to realistic (tens-to-hundreds) asset universes are not demonstrated.

#limitation:noise — Hardware noise effects are explored (hardware vs noise-free MPS), and results indicate sensitivity to noise; practical performance depends on NISQ device quality and scheduling (heavy-hex Rzz layers).

#limitation:data-encoding — The paper uses binary selection with normalization w = x/||x||_1 and a weighted-sum scalarization; no detailed analysis of encoding overheads or impact on large-n encoding is provided.
contradictions: contradiction:scalability — The paper claims practical multi-objective portfolio discovery benefits from QAOA but demonstrates results only on a small 10-asset universe using a 42-qubit subgraph and pre-trained parameters; this raises doubt about scalability to realistic portfolio sizes and whether the reported quantum advantage holds at larger n.

contradiction:classical-vs-quantum — Runtime and sample-efficiency comparisons favor QAMOO, but the experimental setup uses pre-trained QAOA parameters (no per-instance classical optimization) and heavy classical preprocessing/postprocessing (Dirichlet sampling, archive maintenance). This makes it unclear whether the advantage stems from quantum processing alone or from hybrid design choices and parameter transfer, potentially biasing comparisons with classical multi-objective optimizers.
